what: This run is a stand-in that proves the machinery. No training vectors were published when it ran, so two thirds of the `val` photos were used to fit the heads and the last third to choose settings. With about two fitting photos a species, these numbers say little about what the real training set (up to sixty photos a species) will give. They are here to show that every step runs and to be replaced.

notes: The map into BioCLIP 2's space was fitted on 1226 pairs of vectors of the same photos.

The extra set's vectors were not published for this model when this ran, so no kind row could be fitted for `person` or `none`. The sentence rows for the two are kept beside the trained rows, with a bias set on the tuning photos so that at most 0.5% of them are called `person` or `none`. How often a person is then called a person is unmeasured.

The extra set's vectors (people, pets, livestock, rooms) were not published for this model when this ran, so the kind decision was tuned on wildlife photos alone and says nothing about a person or an empty room.

confidence.head: prototypes + sentences
confidence.text: For the head `prototypes + sentences`, the scale was set on the tuning photos (expected calibration error 0.106 there). A species is named when its probability is at least 0.90, the lowest level from which named species were right at least nine times in ten on the tuning photos; three species are offered when the first three together reach 0.94, set the same way. On the test photos a species is then named for 14.3% (13.3 to 15.4) of photos and that name is right for 91.9% (89.7 to 93.8) of them; three species are offered for 9.0% (8.2 to 9.9) and hold the right one for 90.2% (87.3 to 93.1); 76.6% (75.3 to 77.9) get a kind of eye only. These figures leave out the page's rule that names and offers must agree with the winning kind; the exported slot is scored with that rule.
